title: Mathlib Imports
content: Imports natural number basics with primality, finite sets, real numbers, and tactics. The primality import is essential for the representation constraint $m = p \cdot a$ with $p$ prime, while real numbers are needed for the reciprocal sum $\sum 1/n$.
mathContext: Requires $\text{Nat.Prime}$, $\text{Finset.filter}$, $\text{Real.log}$ for primality testing, subset counting, and logarithmic bounds.

title: Representation Count and Bounded Representations
content: reprCount A m counts elements $a \in A$ such that $m = p \cdot a$ for some prime $p$ — the number of ways to write $m$ as a prime multiple of an element of $A$. HasBoundedRepr A r requires $\text{reprCount}(A, m) \leq r$ for all $m$. This is the central constraint of the problem: bounding the 'multiplicative overlap' between $A$ and the primes.
mathContext: $\text{reprCount}(A, m) = |\{a \in A : \exists p \text{ prime},\; m = p \cdot a\}|$; $\text{HasBoundedRepr}(A, r) \iff \forall m,\; \text{reprCount}(A, m) \leq r$

title: Basic Properties of Representation Count
content: Four proved theorems establishing the basic algebra of reprCount and HasBoundedRepr: (1) the empty set has reprCount 0, (2) reprCount is bounded by $|A|$, (3) the empty set has $r$-bounded representations for all $r$, (4) HasBoundedRepr is monotone in $r$ and hereditary under subsets. These are the non-trivial proved results in the file.
mathContext: Proved: $\text{reprCount}(\emptyset, m) = 0$; $\text{reprCount}(A, m) \leq |A|$; $r$-bounded $\implies r'$-bounded for $r' \geq r$; $A \subseteq B$ and $B$ $r$-bounded $\implies A$ $r$-bounded

title: Reciprocal Sum and Its Properties
content: reciprocalSum A computes $\sum_{n \in A} 1/n$ (treating $n = 0$ as contributing 0). The file proves three properties: the empty sum is 0, the sum is non-negative, and it is monotone under subset inclusion. It also shows that inserting a positive element increases the sum by $1/n$. These are proved theorems using Finset.sum lemmas.
mathContext: $\text{reciprocalSum}(A) = \sum_{n \in A} \frac{1}{n}$; proved: non-negative, monotone, additive on insertion

title: Erdős Problem 538
content: The problem asks for the optimal function $f(r, N)$ bounding the reciprocal sum: $\sum_{n \in A} 1/n \leq f(r, N)$ whenever $A \subseteq \{1, \ldots, N\}$ has $r$-bounded representations, and $f$ is minimal among all such bounds. The formalization captures both the upper bound property and the optimality condition ($f \leq g$ for any other valid bound $g$).
mathContext: $\text{ErdosProblem538} \iff \exists f^*,\; \forall A \text{ with } r\text{-bounded repr},\; \sum 1/n \leq f^*(r,N) \text{ and } f^* \text{ is minimal}$

title: Erdős Upper Bound: $O(r \cdot \log N / \log\log N)$
content: Erdős proved by double counting that $\sum_{n \in A} 1/n \leq C \cdot r \cdot \log N / \log\log N$. The argument: multiply the reciprocal sum by $\sum_{p \leq N} 1/p \sim \log\log N$ (Mertens' theorem). Each resulting term $1/(pa)$ with $pa \leq N$ corresponds to a representation, and the $r$-bounded constraint limits the total. The harmonic sum $\sum_{m \leq N} 1/m \sim \log N$ then gives the result. This theorem has a sorry — the proof requires Mertens' theorem which is deep.
mathContext: $\sum_{n \in A} \frac{1}{n} \leq C \cdot r \cdot \frac{\log N}{\log\log N}$; proof via $(\sum 1/a)(\sum_{p} 1/p) \leq r \cdot \sum_{m} 1/m$

title: Double Counting Framework
content: The combinatorial core of Erdős's argument. For each $a \in A$, the number of primes $p$ with $pa \leq N$ is at most $N/a$ (sorry — requires prime counting). Summing $\text{reprCount}(A, m)$ over $m$ gives at most $|A| \cdot N$ since each $a$ contributes at most $N/a \leq N$ representations. Both theorems have sorries as they require non-trivial bounds on prime counting functions.
mathContext: $|\{p \text{ prime} : pa \leq N\}| \leq N/a$; $\sum_{m \leq N} \text{reprCount}(A, m) \leq |A| \cdot N$

title: Multiplicative Energy Bound
content: The representation constraint bounds the multiplicative energy of $A$ with the primes: the number of pairs $(a_1, a_2) \in A \times A$ with $q_1 a_1 = q_2 a_2$ for primes $q_1, q_2$ is at most $r^2 |A|$. This connects Problem 538 to the broader multiplicative energy framework in additive combinatorics. The theorem has a sorry.
mathContext: $|\{(a_1, a_2) \in A^2 : \exists q_1, q_2 \text{ prime},\; q_1 a_1 = q_2 a_2\}| \leq r^2 |A|$

title: Special Cases: $r = 1$ and Singletons
content: For $r = 1$, each integer $m$ has at most one representation $m = pa$ with $a \in A$, forcing $A$ to be 'multiplicatively thin'. The trivial bound $|A| \leq N$ is proved (via subset of $\{0, \ldots, N\}$). A singleton set $\{a\}$ always has 1-bounded representations (proved: at most one element passes the filter). Both are fully proved without sorry.
